sn12.17:1.2: The Exalted One was once staying near Rajagaha, in the Bamboo Grove at the Squirrels' Feeding-Ground.
sn12.17:1.3: Now the Exalted One in the early morning dressed himself, and taking bowl and robe entered Rājagaha for alms.
sn12.17:1.4: And Kassapa the Unclothed saw the Exalted One coming from afar,
sn12.17:1.5: and seeing him he came up to the Exalted One and greeted him,
sn12.17:1.6: and when compliments of friendship and courtesy had been exchanged, he stood at one side. So standing Kassapa the Unclothed said:—
sn12.17:1.7: “We will ask Master Gotama concerning one point, if he would give us opportunity of hearing him reply to our question.”
sn12.17:1.8: “It is untimely just now for questions, Kassapa.
sn12.17:2.5: But Kassapa made his request again. And again, and even a third time he received the same reply.
sn12.17:2.7: When the Exalted One had thus spoken, Kassapa the Unclothed said:—
sn12.17:2.8: “It is not many things we want to ask of Master Gotama.”
sn12.17:3.1: “Now then, Master Gotama, is suffering wrought by one's self?”
sn12.17:3.2: “Not so, Kassapa,” said the Exalted One.
sn12.17:3.3: “What then, Master Gotama, is one's suffering wrought by another?”
sn12.17:3.4: “Not so, Kassapa,” said the Exalted One.
sn12.17:3.5: “What then, Master Gotama, is suffering wrought both by one's self and by another?'
sn12.17:3.6: “Not so, Kassapa,” said the Exalted One.
sn12.17:3.7: “What then, Master Gotama, has [the] suffering [which is] wrought neither by myself nor by another, befallen me by chance?”
sn12.17:3.8: “Not so, Kassapa,” said the Exalted One.
sn12.17:3.9: “What then, Master Gotama, is suffering non-existent?”
sn12.17:3.12: “Then Master Gotama neither knows nor sees suffering.”
sn12.17:3.13: “No, Kassapa, I am not one who knows not suffering nor sees it.
sn12.17:3.14: I am one that knows suffering, Kassapa,
sn12.17:3.15: I am one that sees suffering.”
sn12.17:4.1: “How now, Master Gotama? To all my questions you have said 'not so verily.”
sn12.17:4.5: You have both affirmed that suffering is,
sn12.17:4.9: Declare then to me, Master, Exalted One, [the nature of] suffering.
sn12.17:4.10: Teach me, Master, Exalted One, the nature of suffering.”
sn12.17:5.1: “One and the same person both acts and experiences [the results]':—this, Kassapa, which you called at first 'suffering self-wrought,' amounts to the Eternalist theory.
sn12.17:5.2: “One acts, another experiences [the result]':—this, Kassapa, which to one smitten by the feeling occurs as 'suffering caused by another,' amounts to the Annihilationist theory.
sn12.17:5.3: To you, Kassapa, the Tathagata, not approaching either extreme, teaches the Norm by a middle [way]:—
sn12.17:5.4: conditioned by ignorance activities come to pass,
sn12.17:5.6: thus arise name-and-shape, sense, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, decay-and-death, grief, suffering.
sn12.17:5.7: But from the utter fading away and ceasing of ignorance,
sn12.17:5.8: activities and the rest, comes the ceasing of activities, consciousness and the rest.
sn12.17:5.9: Even such is the ceasing of this entire mass of ill.”
sn12.17:6.1: When this had been said Kassapa the Unclothed said to the Exalted One:—
sn12.17:6.3: Just as if a man were to set up that which had been thrown down, or were to reveal that which was hidden away, or were to point out the right road to him who had gone astray, or were to bring a lamp into the darkness, so that those who had eyes could see shapes,—even so, lord, has the lord Gotama shown me his doctrine in various ways.
sn12.17:6.4: I, even I, lord, betake myself to the Exalted One as my refuge, to the Norm and to the Order.
sn12.17:6.5: I would leave the world under the Rule of the Exalted One. I would be ordained.”
sn12.17:7.1: “He, Kassapa, who, being formerly a votary of another doctrine, desires to leave the world to obtain orders in this Doctrine and Rule, remains on probation for four months. At the end of four months spent in seclusion, the brethren, moved in heart and will, receive him from the world and ordain him to be a brother.
sn12.17:7.2: Nevertheless, I acknowledge a difference in persons.”
sn12.17:8.1: “If, lord, he who, formerly a votary of another doctrine, desires to leave the world, to obtain orders in this Doctrine and Rule, goes on probation for four months, and if at the end of four months spent in seclusion, the brethren, moved in heart and willing, receive him from the world and ordain him to be a brother, I will live on probation for four years. At the end of four years so living may the brethren, moved in heart and will, receive me and ordain me as a brother.”
sn12.17:9.1: So Kassapa the Unclothed was received under the Exalted One and obtained ordination.
sn12.17:9.2: And not long after his ordination the venerable Kassapa, remaining alone and separate, earnest, ardent and strenuous, attained ere long to that supreme goal of the divine life, for the sake of which the clansmen rightly go forth from home into the homeless: yea, that supreme goal did he, by himself, even in this present life, come to understand and realize,
sn12.17:9.3: namely, that birth was destroyed, that the divine life was lived, that the task was done, that for life in these conditions there was no hereafter.
sn12.17:9.4: And that venerable Kassapa became one of the Arahants.
